name: Etori
summary: Japanese partnership trick-taking game where teams compete to capture A K Q J picture cards, called Egara.
rules_text: 4 or 6 players form fixed pairs opposite each other; in 6-player only 4 play each hand, the third pair deals and sits out. A 52-card deck is split between the two dealers and dealt one by one counter-clockwise into 4 piles of 13; the pile with the last card (Kirijimai) goes to a designated active player and the rest clockwise. Trump suit (Kiri) starts as spades and may be changed by dealers before any hand is looked at. The Ace of Spades (or Ace of Clubs when spades are trump) is Rensho: it always wins its trick but belongs to its printed suit. Play is counter-clockwise, must follow suit if able otherwise discard. Highest Rensho wins, else highest trump, else highest of led suit wins trick and leads next. Picture cards taken are kept face-up. Partnership taking 9+ of the 16 pictures wins the hand, 8-8 loses if they hold Rensho. Winners take Go stones from losers: 1 to 4 stones based on how many pictures taken and whether they started with no aces or without Rensho and trump ace.
rating_reason: Japanese trick-taking with trumps and counters, specific and playable
